vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who teaches at a school
vocabulary.example: My teacher explains grammar very clearly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who treats sick people
vocabulary.example: You should see a doctor about that cough.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who cares for sick people in a hospital
vocabulary.example: The nurse checked my temperature.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who designs and builds machines, roads or bridges
vocabulary.example: Omar wants to be an engineer and design bridges.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who drives a vehicle as a job
vocabulary.example: The bus driver said good morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a member of the police
vocabulary.note_ar: مصطلح محايد بدل policeman. في بريطانيا يُسمَّون بالعامية bobbies نسبة إلى Robert Peel مؤسس شرطة لندن
vocabulary.example: A police officer helped us find the way.
vocabulary.note_en: A neutral word used instead of "policeman". In Britain, police officers are informally called "bobbies", after Robert Peel, who founded the London police.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person whose job is to put out fires
vocabulary.note_ar: firefighter الكلمة الشائعة اليوم، و fireman الكلمة الأقدم
vocabulary.example: The firefighters arrived in five minutes.
vocabulary.note_en: "Firefighter" is the common word today; "fireman" is the older word.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a professional cook in a restaurant
vocabulary.example: The chef tasted the soup before serving it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who brings food to tables in a restaurant
vocabulary.note_ar: waitress للمؤنث، server الكلمة المحايدة الحديثة
vocabulary.example: The waiter brought us the menu.
vocabulary.note_en: "Waitress" is for a woman; "server" is the modern neutral word for anyone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who grows crops or keeps animals
vocabulary.example: The farmer gets up very early.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person whose job is to give legal advice
vocabulary.example: The lawyer gave us advice about the contract.
vocabulary.note_en: law = the rules of a country; a lawyer works with the law.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who designs buildings and watches their construction
vocabulary.example: An architect designed this beautiful museum.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who writes news for newspapers or websites
vocabulary.example: A journalist wrote a report about the fair.
vocabulary.note_en: A journal is a magazine or newspaper.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who keeps and checks money records
vocabulary.example: Our accountant checks the company's taxes.
vocabulary.note_en: An account is a record of money; an accountant keeps these records.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who controls a team or department
vocabulary.example: The manager is thinking of hiring a new engineer.
vocabulary.note_en: manage = to control or run something.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an expert who studies nature through experiments
vocabulary.example: The scientist works in a laboratory.
vocabulary.note_en: science → scientist (a person who works in science).

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who flies a plane
vocabulary.example: The pilot welcomed us on board.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who plans how things will look
vocabulary.example: She is a fashion designer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the long-term progress of your working life over many years
vocabulary.example: She built an impressive career in medicine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a job that needs advanced study, training and official qualifications
vocabulary.example: Medicine and law are respected professions.
vocabulary.note_en: This is where the word "professional" comes from.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the official name for the job you do, used on forms
vocabulary.example: Please write your occupation on this form.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who works for a company
vocabulary.example: The company has 200 employees.
vocabulary.note_en: employee = the person who works for a company; employer = the person or company that gives the job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person or company that gives people jobs
vocabulary.example: More than 50 employers came to the career fair.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you work with in the same profession
vocabulary.example: I had lunch with my colleagues.
vocabulary.note_en: The "ue" at the end is silent: /ˈkɒliːɡ/

vocabulary.meaning_en: all the people who work for a company
vocabulary.example: The hotel staff were very friendly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a group of people who work together
vocabulary.example: Our team finished the project early.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a business that makes or sells things
vocabulary.example: He works for a big software company.

vocabulary.meaning_en: working all the normal hours, about 40 a week
vocabulary.example: She has a full-time job at the bank.

vocabulary.meaning_en: working only some hours or days a week
vocabulary.example: He has a part-time job at a bookshop.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having the ability to do something well
vocabulary.example: We need a skilled driver for this job.
vocabulary.note_en: skill = an ability you learn and practise.

vocabulary.meaning_en: doing your work with high quality and commitment
vocabulary.example: She is very professional with her clients.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a lot of knowledge from doing something
vocabulary.example: We are looking for an experienced nurse.
vocabulary.note_en: experience = the knowledge you get from doing something for a long time.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a natural ability to do something very well
vocabulary.example: Ali is a talented designer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an event where companies meet people looking for jobs
vocabulary.example: I met three employers at the career fair.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small area at a fair for one company
vocabulary.example: The engineering booth was very busy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who is looking for a job
vocabulary.example: The fair was full of students and job seekers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a document that lists your education and work experience
vocabulary.example: Send your resume to the manager.
vocabulary.note_en: American English; in British English it is a CV.

fine_lines.title: job vs career vs profession vs occupation
fine_lines.explanation_ar: job الوظيفة المحددة التي تقوم بها لتكسب المال، وقد تكون مؤقتة. career المسار المهني الطويل عبر سنوات حياتك والترقيات. profession مهنة تخصصية تحتاج دراسة أكاديمية متقدمة وتراخيص رسمية مثل الطب والمحاماة. occupation المصطلح الرسمي المحايد الذي تكتبه في الاستمارات الرسمية في البنك أو السفر.

examples.sentence: He has a part-time job at a bookstore.
She built an impressive career in international medicine.
Medicine, law and architecture are respected professions.
Please write your current occupation on this form.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A job is the specific work you do to earn money, and it can be temporary. A career is your long working path over many years, with promotions. A profession is specialised work that needs advanced study and official licences, like medicine or law. Occupation is the formal, neutral word you write on official forms, for example at the bank or when you travel.

fine_lines.title: colleague vs co-worker
fine_lines.explanation_ar: co-worker أي شخص يعمل معك في نفس المبنى أو مكان العمل حتى لو في قسم مختلف. colleague زميل في نفس التخصص المهني أو المستوى العلمي، وتحمل احتراماً مهنياً أكبر.

examples.sentence: We share an office with ten co-workers from the sales department.
Dr Omar discussed the research with his hospital colleagues.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A co-worker is anyone who works with you in the same building or workplace, even in a different department. A colleague works in the same professional field or at the same level, and the word sounds more respectful and professional.

fine_lines.title: employee vs employer
fine_lines.explanation_ar: اللاحقة ee تدل على الشخص الذي يقع عليه الفعل (الموظف الذي يتم توظيفه)، واللاحقة er تدل على من يقوم بالفعل (صاحب العمل الذي يوظّف).

examples.sentence: Every new employee gets a laptop.
My employer pays me at the end of each month.

fine_lines.explanation_en: The ending -ee shows the person who receives the action (the employee is the one who is employed). The ending -er shows the person who does the action (the employer is the one who employs).

expressions.meaning_ar: يتعلم أصول العمل الجديد وكيفية أداء المهام
expressions.example: It takes a few weeks for any new employee to learn the ropes.
expressions.meaning_en: to learn how a new job works and how to do the tasks

expressions.meaning_ar: يجمع أشخاصاً مختلفين في مكان واحد
expressions.example: The fair brought together students and companies.
expressions.meaning_en: to bring different people together in one place

expressions.example: Let's get straight to business and start the meeting.
expressions.meaning_en: to start talking about the main topic immediately

expressions.example: Omar likes engineering. Ali, on the other hand, loves design.
expressions.meaning_en: used to show a different or opposite idea

expressions.example: I'm having a great time at my new job.

grammar.title: Verbs that change meaning with -ing: think and have
grammar.explanation_ar: بعض الأفعال تكون أفعال حالة في معنى، وأفعال حركة في معنى آخر. think بمعنى يعتقد (رأي ثابت) لا تأخذ ing، لكن بمعنى يفكر الآن تأخذ ing. have بمعنى يمتلك لا تأخذ ing، لكن بمعنى يتناول وجبة أو يمر بتجربة تأخذ ing.
examples: I think this job is excellent. / I am thinking about the new job offer.
She has a successful company. / We are having lunch with the manager.
Ali is having a great time at the fair.
grammar.explanation_en: Some verbs are state verbs with one meaning and action verbs with another meaning. "Think" meaning "believe" (a fixed opinion) doesn't take -ing, but "think" meaning "consider something right now" does. "Have" meaning "own" doesn't take -ing, but "have" meaning "eat a meal" or "go through an experience" does.

grammar.title: Verbs that change meaning with -ing: see, taste and smell
grammar.explanation_ar: see بمعنى يرى بعينه أو يفهم لا تأخذ ing، لكن بمعنى يقابل شخصاً في موعد تأخذ ing. taste و smell كصفة للطعام لا تأخذ ing، لكن عندما يقوم الشخص بفعل التذوق أو الشم بنفسه تأخذ ing.
examples: I see what you mean. / The lawyer is seeing a new client this afternoon.
The soup smells good. / The chef is smelling the soup.
The food tastes great. / He is tasting the sauce.
grammar.explanation_en: "See" meaning "look with your eyes" or "understand" doesn't take -ing, but "see" meaning "meet someone at an appointment" does. "Taste" and "smell" describing food don't take -ing, but when a person is actively tasting or smelling something, they take -ing.

questions.question: Which word do you write on official forms for your job?
questions.explanation_en: "Occupation" is the formal word used on official forms.

questions.question: "She built an impressive ___ in medicine over 30 years."
questions.explanation_ar: career = المسار المهني الطويل عبر السنين.
questions.explanation_en: Career = your long working path over many years.

questions.question: The manager is sitting and considering it right now: "The manager ___ of hiring a new engineer."
questions.explanation_ar: think بمعنى يفكر الآن فعل حركة يأخذ ing.
questions.explanation_en: "Think" meaning "consider right now" is an action, so it takes -ing.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation_ar: smell كصفة للشيء فعل حالة لا يأخذ ing.
questions.explanation_en: "Smell" describing what something is like is a state verb, so it doesn't take -ing.

questions.question: "The lawyer is seeing a new client this afternoon." Here "seeing" means:
questions.explanation_ar: see بمعنى يقابل في موعد يأخذ ing.

questions.question: "Learn the ropes" means:
choices: learn how to do a new job
questions.explanation_ar: learn the ropes = يتعلم أصول العمل الجديد.
questions.explanation_en: "Learn the ropes" = to learn how a new job works.

questions.question: A person who designs buildings is an:
questions.explanation_ar: architect = مهندس معماري، و ch تُنطق k.
questions.explanation_en: An architect designs buildings, and the "ch" is pronounced like "k".

questions.question: The company that gives you a job is your:
questions.explanation_en: Employer = the person or company that gives you a job; employee = the worker.

questions.question: Which job needs advanced study and an official license?
choices: a part-time job in a shop
questions.explanation_ar: profession مهنة تحتاج دراسة وتراخيص رسمية.
questions.explanation_en: A profession needs advanced study and official licences.
